title: Vectored residency orchestrator and GPU page admission control for blocked-KV runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As blocked/paged KV cache is used to enable working sets larger than GPU memory, we observe two recurring issues: (1) tail-latency spikes from synchronous page admission under heavy continuous-batching load, and (2) tenant unfairness where noisy tenants evict other tenants' hot pages via aggressive admission behavior. Goal: design and implement a vectored residency orchestrator plus a GPU page admission controller that reduces p95 generation latency by limiting synchronous page swaps, enforces soft residency budgets per-tenant and per-model, and coordinates admission across concurrent batch lanes. This ticket covers the design, prototype implementation, test harness, and canary rollout configuration for runtime-1.24.
technical_decisions: Admission controller runs in the host-side dispatcher and makes per-request admission decisions before enqueuing page transfers.
Represent contiguous page groups as 'vectors' (small fixed-size multi-page descriptors) to amortize PCIe transfer setup and reduce scatter-gather overhead.
Use a lightweight residency estimator based on sliding-window token access counts (token-affinity lanes) to prioritize hot vectors.
Enforce soft-residency budgets (byte quotas) per-tenant and a global per-GPU admission watermark with hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
Eviction is decoupled: evict decisions are scheduled async and use batched writeback where necessary to avoid synchronous stalls during admission.
Fallback policy: if admission would exceed budget and eviction cannot free enough space within a short deadline, route the request to slower compatible model variant or host-emulated KV path.
Telemetry: emit per-admission reason codes, vector transfer sizes, admit latency, and evict latency for observability and tuning.
Runtime knobs: admission window (ms), vector size (pages), per-tenant budget (MB), admission backoff strategy (exponential vs linear).
Do not modify kernel scheduler/prefetch kernel selection in this ticket; focus on orchestration and admission control only.
design_notes: Vectorized residency: group 4-8 adjacent pages into a single vector descriptor. Each vector has hot-score, last-access-ts, and owner-tenant tag.

Admission flow: request arrives -> residency estimator computes vector candidates -> admission controller simulates budget impact -> if accepted, enqueue DMA for vector -> append to batch lane; if rejected, apply fallback policy.
Budget model: use exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) to smooth short bursts and allocate headroom for continuous-batching spikes.
Fairness: implement proportional-share admission by tracking tenant credits; credits refill according to configured share weights.
Backpressure signals: when GPU watermark reached, short-circuit admission to force routing to host-emulated path for low-priority traffic.
Eviction heuristics: prefer stale vectors with low hot-score; avoid evicting vectors with active KV pin leases used by in-flight batches.
Instrumentation: sample page fault traces to build a vector-access frequency histogram used by offline tuning job.
tradeoffs: Grouping pages into vectors reduces DMA overhead but may transfer a few cold pages, increasing host->GPU bandwidth usage.
Soft-residency budgets reduce tail OOMs but can increase rejection/fallback rate for aggressive tenants; tuning required to avoid customer-visible regressions.
Decoupling eviction avoids stalls but can temporarily increase peak memory usage until eviction completes.
Host-side admission adds CPU latency and complexity to dispatcher but centralizes fairness and telemetry and avoids in-GPU kernel stalls.
metrics_and_slo_targets: Generation latencies: target p50 <= configured SLO (baseline), p95 improvement >= 30% vs current blocked admission under 80% GPU utilization.
GPU OOMs: reduce OOM rate to <0.01 events/hour per cluster for canary workloads.
Swap I/O: limit sustained PCIe transfer bandwidth per GPU from vector admission to configurable threshold (MB/s) to protect tails.
Fallback rate: track fraction of requests routed to fallback path and keep <5% for production workloads after tuning.
Fairness: no tenant should consume >2x its configured share for longer than 60s without admin override.
testing_plan: Unit tests for residency estimator, vector descriptor lifecycle, and budget accounting.
Microbenchmarks: synthetic traces to measure vector transfer amortization and DMA setup cost reduction.
Trace-driven simulator: replay production KV access traces to validate eviction churn, admission decisions, and bandwidth usage.
Canary: staged rollout on a subset of Dedicated clusters with feature flag; compare latency and OOM metrics against matched control group.
Chaos tests: inject delayed DMA completion and forced host writeback failures to validate graceful fallback behavior.
rollout_and_migration: Feature flag 'vectored-admission-v1' toggles admission controller behavior; default OFF for existing clusters.
Config profile contains vector_size, tenant_budget_mb, admit_window_ms, and backoff_policy.
Start with conservative defaults (vector_size=4, tenant_budget=25% of GPU memory, admit_window=8ms) and adjust after canary telemetry.
Provide telemetry dashboard comparing control vs canary: p50/p95 generation latency, vector admission rate, fallback rate, eviction latency.
Migration: gradual increase of canary traffic share over 2 weeks; automatic rollback on threshold breaches (p95 degradation > 15% or OOM spike).
open_questions: What's the optimal vector size across model families (LLama-like vs decoder-only with long context)? Need offline sweep.
How aggressive should eviction be when multiple tenants simultaneously exceed soft budgets? Consider global victim selection policy.
Should we expose tenant budgets in Console or keep them admin-config-only initially?
Edge-case: handling pinned pages that are in-use by long-running generation; how to preempt safely if budget exhausted?
Integration with quantized sparse-retention window designs — any conflicts with vectorized grouping?
acceptance_criteria: Implementation merged with unit and integration tests covering admission + eviction paths.
Canary shows >=30% reduction in generation p95 under synthetic continuous-batching load at 80% GPU utilization compared to baseline.
Fallback rate under production traces <5% and no increase in user-facing error rates.
No regressions in throughput for low-latency tenants; telemetry confirms tenant fairness behavior.
Operational runbook updated and SRE reviewed, including kill-switch and rollback plan.
